mainTopic: The two names of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, how witnesses' 'I do not know' affects their testimony in חקירות and בדיקות, how long a date mix-up is excused, and how long one may bless the new moon.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation: the משנה calls him 'בן זכאי' and a ברייתא calls him 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי' because one name is from his student years and the other from his teaching years. The גמרא then asks why the משנה needs to say that in בדיקות the testimony stands 'even if two' witnesses do not know. רב ששת connects the phrase to חקירות, following רבי עקיבא. רבא rejects that reading and explains that even in חקירות, two witnesses who know are enough, which is not like רבי עקיבא. In a story, רמי בר חמא asks רב כהנא and רב ספרא why חקירות and בדיקות are treated differently when both come from the Torah. They answer that without time and place the testimony cannot be checked through הזמה, but missing side details still leave הזמה possible. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that witnesses who are one day apart can be excused only until most of the month has passed. רבא tries to prove this from the משנה, but the proof is pushed off with the reasoning about שופר blasts. The amud ends with another teaching from רבי יוחנן: the blessing on the new moon may be said until it is filled in, which is either seven days or sixteen days.

steps.title: His name changed when he went from student to teacher
steps.stepSummary: The teaching was recorded under his name. As a student he was called 'בן זכאי', and as a teacher he was called 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they recorded it in his name. When he was a student, people called him 'בן זכאי,' the way you refer to a student sitting before his teacher. When he became a teacher, they called him 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to why one source calls him 'בן זכאי' and another calls him 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי'. It explains that his name changed over the course of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two names do not point to two different people. 'בן זכאי' was how a student was referred to, without a title. Once he taught others, he was given the full title 'רבן'.

keyTerms.meaning: They recorded it under his name
An honorary title for a great teacher and leader

phrases.english: And they established it in his name.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה recorded this story under his name.

phrases.english: When he was studying,
they would call him 'Ben Zakkai,'
like a student sitting before his teacher.
When he was teaching,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי״.
phrases.english: they would call him 'Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an answer that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the two names as two stages of one person's life
steps.terutzMaskana: The two names refer to the same person at different stages: student and teacher.

steps.title: Each source uses the name from a different stage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the earlier name 'בן זכאי', and the ברייתא uses his later name 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה calls him 'בן זכאי,' it uses the name he had at first. When the other source calls him 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי,' it uses the name he has now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the explanation from step 1 to the two sources. This removes the apparent contradiction between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the name from back then, when he was a student. The ברייתא uses the name from later, after he became a teacher. Both sources describe the same man, so they do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of / based on the name

steps.whatToRemember: 'בן זכאי' and 'רבן יוחנן בן זכאי' are the same person. One name is from when he was a student, and the other is from when he was a teacher.

phrases.english: When it calls him 'Ben Zakkai' –
phrases.notes: This is the משנה, which calls him just 'בן זכאי.'

phrases.english: it is based on [the name he had] at first,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי״ –
phrases.english: and when it calls him 'Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai' –
it is based on [the name he has] now.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״בֶּן זַכַּאי״ – עַל שֵׁם דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the naming explanation to the two conflicting sources.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no contradiction. The two sources use names from different stages of his life.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about questioning witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the next lines of the משנה: the story of the examination, and the difference between חקירות and בדיקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'There was an incident, and he examined…' and 'What is the difference between חקירות…'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה so that it can ask a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, if one witness says 'I do not know' to a חקירה (a core question), the testimony is void. For a בדיקה (a side detail), the testimony stands even if one witness says 'I do not know,' and the משנה adds 'even if two say so.' That added phrase is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Core questions put to witnesses (when and where), which they must answer
'Etc.': the quote is only the opening words

phrases.english: 'An incident occurred, and he examined,' etc.
'What is the difference between interrogations,' etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה וּבָדַק כּוּ׳. מָה בֵּין חֲקִירוֹת כּוּ׳.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In חקירות, one witness saying 'I do not know' voids the testimony. In בדיקות, the testimony stands even if one or two witnesses say 'I do not know.'

steps.title: Why say 'even if two'? It's obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the testimony stands in בדיקות when one witness doesn't know, then of course it stands when two don't know. So why does the משנה add 'even two'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'even if two say' add? It's obvious! If the testimony stands when one witness says 'I don't know,' then it also stands when two say so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the extra phrase in the משנה as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already showed that not knowing a בדיקה does not hurt the testimony. Then the number of witnesses who don't know shouldn't matter, so 'even two' teaches nothing new. The גמרא assumes every phrase in a משנה must teach something.

phrases.english: What is [the point of] 'even if two say'?
It is obvious!
If when one says 'I do not know' –
their testimony stands,
then when two say [it],
their testimony also stands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks a phrase in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'even if two say' in the בדיקות clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If not knowing a בדיקה doesn't disqualify one witness, it can't disqualify two either. So the phrase adds nothing.

steps.title: רב ששת: the phrase belongs to the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says 'even two' goes back to חקירות. Even if two witnesses know and a third doesn't, the whole testimony is void. This follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The phrase refers back to the first part of the משנה. It means: in חקירות, even if two witnesses say 'We know' and one says 'I don't know,' their testimony is void. Whose view is this? רבי עקיבא's, who treats a group of three witnesses like a pair of two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by moving 'even two' back to the חקירות clause. He then names the תנא whose view this follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, 'even two' teaches something new: two good witnesses do not save the testimony if a third witness fails a חקירה. That only makes sense for רבי עקיבא, who holds that three witnesses are one group, just like two. If one of them fails, the whole group fails.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to the first clause

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'two' means two witnesses who DO know the answer, not two who don't. The problem is the third witness who doesn't know.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It refers to the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the part about חקירות.

phrases.english: and this is what it is saying:
In the interrogations, even if two say 'We know'
and one says 'I do not know' –
their testimony is void.
In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
who compares three [witnesses] to two.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attaching the phrase to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Even two' belonged to the בדיקות clause and was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Even two' belongs to חקירות: two who know cannot save testimony when a third doesn't know. This follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבא: but the משנה says the testimony stands
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the משנה's words are 'their testimony stands,' not 'is void,' so רב ששת's reading doesn't fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But the משנה teaches 'their testimony stands'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב ששת's reading because it contradicts the actual words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's reading has the משנה ruling that the testimony is void. But the phrase 'even two' sits next to the words 'their testimony stands.' A reading cannot reverse the ruling that the משנה states.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (pointing to the wording of the source)

phrases.english: Rava said:
But it teaches 'their testimony stands'!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ששת's whole reading of the phrase
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It turns 'their testimony stands' into 'their testimony is void.'

steps.title: רבא: even in חקירות, two who know are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the משנה this way: even in חקירות, if two witnesses know and one doesn't, the testimony stands. This is not like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what it means. Even in חקירות, if two say 'We know' and one says 'I don't know,' their testimony stands. Whose view is this? Not רבי עקיבא's.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading. It keeps the words 'their testimony stands' and still gives 'even two' a new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that even in the strict area of חקירות, two witnesses who know are enough, and the third one's ignorance is ignored. This disagrees with רבי עקיבא, who would void the whole group of three.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת: in חקירות, 2 who know + 1 who doesn't = void (like רבי עקיבא). רבא: 2 who know + 1 who doesn't = valid (not like רבי עקיבא).
steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement shows how one phrase in a משנה can decide whether the משנה follows רבי עקיבא's view that three witnesses are judged as one group.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what it is saying:
Even in the interrogations,
if two say 'We know'
and one says 'I do not know' –
their testimony stands.
In accordance with whom? Not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's rejected reading with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the phrase so it keeps the משנה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת: the phrase teaches that the testimony is void, following רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in חקירות, two who know are enough and the testimony stands. This is not like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא meets two students of רבה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב כהנא and רב ספרא what new ideas they learned on סנהדרין in רבה's yeshiva. They answer that it is the same plain סנהדרין, and ask what is bothering him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב ספרא learned מסכת סנהדרין in רבה's yeshiva. רמי בר חמא met them and asked, 'What do you say about סנהדרין, the way it is learned in רבה's yeshiva?' They answered, 'What would we say about it? It is just regular סנהדרין! What is bothering you?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that sets up a new question on the משנה. רמי בר חמא wants to test what the two students learned, and they invite him to ask his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No question on the משנה has been asked yet. Their humble reply, 'it is just plain סנהדרין,' turns the conversation into a request: tell us your specific difficulty. This opens the way for the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he met them / came across them
what is bothering you? / what is your question?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Safra
studied Sanhedrin in the school of Rabba.
Rami bar Chama met them.
He said to them: What do you say about it,
about Sanhedrin of Rabba's school?
They said to him: And what do we say about it,
about plain Sanhedrin?
phrases.notes: They're being modest: it's the same מסכת everyone learns, so there's nothing special to report.

phrases.english: And what is difficult for you?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרִיתוּ בַּהּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין דְּבֵי רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'even two' discussion and opens a new story that will bring a fresh question on the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new insight did the students learn on סנהדרין in רבה's yeshiva?

steps.title: Why are חקירות and בדיקות treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quotes the משנה: one 'I don't know' cancels the testimony in חקירות, but in בדיקות even two do not. Since both kinds of questioning come from the Torah, why the difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'My question is from the משנה that says: What is the difference between חקירות and בדיקות? In חקירות, if one witness says "I don't know," their testimony is cancelled. In בדיקות, if one says "I don't know," and even if two say "we don't know," their testimony still stands. But both kinds of questions are from the Torah! So why are they different?'
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks his question. He points out that the משנה treats two Torah-required kinds of questioning in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both kinds of questioning are required by the Torah, failing either one should seem equally serious. Yet the משנה cancels the testimony over one missing answer in חקירות, while in בדיקות even two missing answers are fine. He wants the reason behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: this one and that one, both
what is different? Why the difference?

phrases.english: He said to them: From that which is taught:
What is the difference between interrogations and examinations?
In interrogations, if one says "I do not know,"
their testimony is void.
In examinations, if one says "I do not know,"
and even if two say "We do not know,"
their testimony stands.
After all, both this and that are from the Torah;

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא חֲקִירוֹת וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּדִיקוֹת?
phrases.english: what is different about interrogations, and what is different about examinations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the specific question the students asked for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's different rulings for חקירות and בדיקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both kinds of questioning are Torah requirements, so an unanswered question should have the same result in both.

steps.title: The difference is whether הזמה is possible
steps.stepSummary: Without the time-and-place answers of חקירות, the testimony can't be made זוממין, so it is invalid. Without side details in בדיקות, הזמה is still possible, so the testimony stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'How can you compare them? In חקירות, if one witness says "I don't know," their testimony is cancelled, because it becomes testimony that you cannot prove false through הזמה. In בדיקות, if one of them says "I don't know," their testimony stands, because it is still testimony that you can prove false through הזמה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא and רב ספרא answer the question. The difference depends on whether the testimony can still be checked through הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony that can never be proven false through הזמה is not valid testimony. חקירות ask for the basic time and place, so a witness who doesn't know them gives testimony that can't be checked, and it falls. בדיקות ask about small side details, so even if those are missing, the time and place are known, הזמה is still possible, and the testimony stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: how can you compare? These are not alike
to make it זוממין, to prove witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at that time
testimony that cannot be proven false through הזמה, which is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not that one kind of question is more 'Torah' than the other. Both are from the Torah. The point is that only missing time-and-place answers make הזמה impossible.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of עדות: valid testimony must be the kind that could be checked through הזמה.

phrases.english: They said to him: How can you compare?
In interrogations, if one says "I do not know,"
their testimony is void,
because it becomes testimony
that you cannot render conspiratory.
phrases.notes: If a witness gives no time or place, nobody can come and say 'he was with us somewhere else then.'

phrases.english: In examinations, if one of them says "I do not know,"
their testimony stands,
since it is testimony that you can render conspiratory.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the two cases differ in whether הזמה remains possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both are from the Torah, a missing answer should matter equally in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only missing time-and-place answers (חקירות) make הזמה impossible, and that is what cancels the testimony.

steps.title: Praise from רמי בר חמא and a humble reply
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא praises the answer. They humbly reply that the answer only seems strong because he was kind enough to accept it; if he had wanted to attack it, it wouldn't hold up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'If this is what you say about it, you have said a lot about it!' They said to him: 'Because of your kindness, sir, it seems we said a lot. If you wanted to attack us, sir, we would not have said even one thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רמי בר חמא accepts and praises the answer, and the students answer modestly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about הזמה is accepted as the explanation for the משנה. The students' reply shows humility: an answer looks strong partly because the asker is willing to accept it.
steps.whatToRemember: In חקירות, one 'I don't know' cancels the testimony because without time and place it cannot be made זוממין. In בדיקות, missing details do not matter, because הזמה is still possible.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי הָכִי אָמְרִיתוּ בַּהּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: If you said like this about it,
you said much about it.
They said to him: Due to the Master's goodness
we said much about it;
with the Master's rebuke,
phrases.notes: They mean: if you had wanted to pick our answer apart, you could have.

phrases.english: we would not have said even one thing about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אָמְרִיתוּ בַּהּ, טוּבָא אָמְרִיתוּ בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רמי בר חמא accepts the answer from step 10, closing the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הזמה explanation is accepted: testimony that cannot be made זוממין is void, which explains the משנה's distinction between חקירות and בדיקות.

steps.title: How far into the month can a witness be confused?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about witnesses who are one day apart and asks how long this excuse works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One says, etc.' Until when does this apply?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה and asks a question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if one witness says 'the second of the month' and the other says 'the third,' the testimony still stands. We assume one witness knew the last month got an extra day and the other did not. The גמרא asks how long into the month we can still say someone did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding an extra day to a month, making it 30 days instead of 29

phrases.english: One says, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: one witness says it happened on the second of the month, the other says the third.

phrases.english: Until how much?
phrases.notes: How many days into the month can we still say a witness didn't know about the extra day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה after the discussion of חקירות and בדיקות ended in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long into the month the court can assume a witness did not know about the extra day added to the previous month.

steps.title: Until most of the month has passed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the excuse works only until most of the month has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: until most of the month has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: A chain of רבנן reports רבי יוחנן's answer: we can say a witness is confused about the date only until the majority of the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Early in the month, a person may not yet have heard that the last month got an extra day. Once most of the month has gone by, we assume he has found out. So after that point, a one-day difference counts as a real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the month (past day 15)

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Until the majority of the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The excuse of not knowing about the extra day works only until most of the month has passed.

steps.title: רבא tries to prove רבי יוחנן's rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the משנה's case of 'the third' versus 'the fifth,' which is void, and says this must be because after most of a month people know the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this in the משנה. If one witness says 'on the third' and one says 'on the fifth,' their testimony is void. Why? Let us say this one knew about two extra days and that one did not! Isn't it because once most of the month has passed, a person knows?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof for רבי יוחנן's rule from another line in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A two-day mistake would mean the witness missed the extra day in both of the last two months. But by the time the second month came, the earlier month was long over, so he would surely have known about it. רבא says the only reason the משנה doesn't accept this excuse is that after most of a month, a person knows.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this (in a משנה)
Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the conclusion of a proof)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned this:
If one says 'on the third'
and one says 'on the fifth,' their testimony is void.
But why?
Let us say that this one knows about two extra days
phrases.notes: Each of the two months before this one got an extra day, so the dates could be off by two.

phrases.english: and that one does not know about the two extra days?
Rather, isn't it because by most of the month he knows!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of Step 13 with a line from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that after most of the month a person knows about the extra day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that 'the third' against 'the fifth' is a void testimony, even though missing two extra days could explain it.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: it's about the שופר, not the time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off רבא's proof: maybe a person can stay confused past most of the month, but he hears the שופר each new month, and he can't miss it twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you: even after most of the month he may not know. But he knows by the שופר. About one שופר blast we can say he made a mistake; about two שופר blasts we cannot say he made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof by giving a different reason for the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ruling does not have to come from 'most of the month.' Each new month was announced with a שופר blast. A person can miss one blast, but not two, so a two-day error is not believable, while a one-day error might last all month.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (introduces a rejection)
The שופר blown to announce the new month

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say רבי יוחנן is wrong. It only says the משנה is not a proof for him, since the משנה can be explained another way.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you:
even by most of the month he does not know,
but he knows by the shofar.
With one shofar, we say he made a mistake;
phrases.notes: He might have missed hearing one new-month blast.

phrases.english: with two shofars, we do not say he made a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought by רבא in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה is rejected; רבי יוחנן's rule itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's ruling can be explained by the two שופר blasts a person would not miss, not by the passing of most of the month.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: a one-day date mix-up is excused only until most of the month. רבא's proof from the משנה is pushed off, because the 'third versus fifth' case can be explained by the two שופר blasts.

steps.title: Blessing the new moon only until it fills out
steps.stepSummary: The same chain of רבנן teaches another rule from רבי יוחנן: one may bless the new moon until it is no longer missing a part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רב אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: Until when may one bless the new month? Until its missing part is filled in.
steps.whatsHappening: Because it just quoted this chain of רבנן, the גמרא brings another teaching of theirs about the blessing on the moon (קידוש לבנה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, linked only by the same names. The rule is that the blessing over the new moon is said only while the moon still looks incomplete; once it looks full, the time is over.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying the blessing on the new moon (קידוש לבנה)
Its missing part / its dent (the part of the moon not yet lit)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Until when may one bless the month?
phrases.notes: This is the blessing said when seeing the new moon.

phrases.english: Until its missing part is filled in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same chain of רבנן as Step 13, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessing on the new moon may be said until the moon no longer looks like it is missing a part.

steps.title: How many days is that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many days it takes until the moon is filled in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many days is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a number of days for רבי יוחנן's rule. This sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until it is filled in' is not exact. The גמרא wants a set number of days in the month.

phrases.english: And how many?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact number of days meant by Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many days into the month the moon counts as 'filled in.'

steps.title: Seven days or sixteen days
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says up to seven days; the רבנן of נהרדעא say up to sixteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רב יהודה: until seven days. The רבנן of נהרדעא say: until sixteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: Two opinions answer the question: seven days, or sixteen days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They argue about what 'filled in' means. רב יהודה gives an early limit of seven days. The נהרדעי allow it until the sixteenth, about when the moon is fully round.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן of the city נהרדעא

steps.whatToRemember: The blessing on the new moon is said until the moon is filled in. רב יהודה: until day seven. נהרדעי: until day sixteen.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yaakov bar Idi said, Rav Yehuda said:
Until seven.
The Nehardeans say: until sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה: until the seventh day. נהרדעי: until the sixteenth day.
